title: Zoom
$requiresComment: Only the access token is presented to api.zoom.us. The client pair and the refresh token belong to the host's OAuth lifecycle, not to an ordinary REST request.

authorize.$comment: Every Zoom REST call is a Bearer token on the Authorization header, OAuth or Server-to-Server alike; this provider declares the user OAuth shape so a host can connect a rep's own Zoom account rather than one shared app-wide identity.

oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: Verified 2026-09-15 against Zoom's own OAuth guide: "You should always use the latest refresh token for the next refresh request" -- a new refresh token is issued on every refresh, and Zoom's docs describe reuse of an old one as an error condition rather than a supported retry path. Refresh tokens themselves last 90 days; access tokens one hour.
oauth.$scopeComment: meeting:read:meeting is what meeting_get needs. user:read:token is what obf_token_create needs -- Zoom's own OBF guide: "Accessing a user's OBF token requires the user:read:token scope." Neither action works without its scope; a host that only asked for one gets a 4xx on the other, not a silent gap.
oauth.$comment: Authorization Code, confidential client. Zoom's PKCE guidance ("Use PKCE to enable user authorization with a public client ID and no client secret") frames it as the PUBLIC-client path; nothing in Zoom's docs requires it of a confidential app that also sends client_secret, unlike Buffer -- so pkce is deliberately not declared here rather than claimed on a guess.

$sandboxComment: UNVERIFIED, not NONE. Zoom documents no separate developer/test estate distinct from a real account -- every OAuth app authorizes against the caller's own live Zoom account, and there is no sandbox toggle in the docs reviewed 2026-09-15. That reads like `none`, but nobody has confirmed there is truly nothing rather than simply not having found it, so the honest value is `unverified` until someone checks directly with a Zoom account.
sandboxNote: Zoom has no test estate distinct from a real account, as far as this review found (2026-09-15) -- but it is UNVERIFIED, not confirmed. Every call authorizes against the caller's own Zoom account and can read real meeting data. Use fake mode while building.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client ID
credentialFields.help: From the Zoom app you registered at marketplace.zoom.us. One value for the whole installation -- the same app serves every connected Zoom account.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client secret
credentialFields.help: From the same app. Used to exchange the code and to refresh; never sent with an API request.

credentialFields.label: Access token
credentialFields.help: Obtained by the host's OAuth exchange, PER CONNECTED ZOOM ACCOUNT. Expires after one hour -- a host that does not refresh will work for a while and then fail with no warning.

credentialFields.label: Refresh token
credentialFields.help: Also per account. A NEW one is issued on every refresh -- persist the replacement atomically, and never retry a refresh that may have already succeeded: replaying an old refresh token is Zoom's own reported failure mode for a rotating grant.
